archived.why: A person must change `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so that `rust (classify)` can finish stage 2 for a change that touches about 20 card scripts. One way is to split stage 2's forced games across parallel jobs. Each card's 40 games are independent, the way `--selfplay-side` split self-play in #2651, and that is the house rule in ci.yml's header ("a piece that grows is split further … never folded back into one long job"). The quicker way is to raise the `rust-classify` job's `timeout-minutes` from 10 to 15 or more. After either change lands, re-run CI on #4090. Its code needs no change.

## Goal

The hourly retention pass deletes cancelled queue tickets, which are dead copies of a player's deck. A new store method `tickets_purge(cutoff)` exists on both stores. It deletes every ticket with `status = 'cancelled'` and `enqueued_at` strictly before the cutoff, and answers the count. It never touches a queued or a claimed ticket. R4446000 records the decision, SPEC §9.5 and the server README say so, and no migration or index is added. Claimed tickets stay, because `matches_mode_of` reads a queue match's mode from its ticket.

## Goal

At each decision's root, the practice AI evolves every readable card that can still evolve, on a sandbox copy:
- every unit on either field;
- every Unit in its own hand, placed on the field first;
- never anything in the enemy's hand.

For each card it records what the evolution changes in its controller's evaluation, as the price of one run of the Evolve text. `unit_worth` then adds `AI_EVAL.evolve` × that price × the number of runs the text would take now (R3536003, so High Evolutionary counts where it acts) × how close the card is to evolving. Closeness is one of:
- the share of its controller's unit zones that are filled;
- the share of the needed (0)-cost cards held (the AI's own cards only);
- the share of its health it has lost;
- `evolve_event_share`, for a card that waits on an event.

Setup moves (filling a zone), guarding a near-evolved unit and answering one (Polymorph) then come out of the existing priced search and move order. There is one ruling (R4648000), every number is a named constant, `evolve` at 0 is the one switch (`GREEDY_EVAL` keeps 0), and nothing hidden is read.

## Steps

**Where this departs from the earlier plan, and why:**
- **The condition is classified once, at the root.** It is stored in the price entry. The earlier plan cloned the game state inside `unit_worth`, which runs at every search node.
- **The baseline is the state before the evolution**, as `hook_firing_price` does, not a hookless twin. A Vanilla twin cannot evolve, so its branch is just the same state settled again.
- **Units in the AI's own hand are priced**, placed first, as R3064000 does. A Drifter played inside a search line then keeps its price.
- **The price is stored per run.** The evolution multiplier then counts wherever it acts.
- **Cards that their own turn or attack text evolves are left to those prices**, so nothing counts twice. These are Wasp, Hornet, Space Invader and Lantern Distiller.
- **No separate on/off bool.** `evolve` at 0 is the switch, as with every other price weight.

# Plan for Issue #4734

## 1. Goal

On a finished game, the board's End turn button reads "Game over" instead of "Enemy turn", carries `data-turn-state="over"`, and remains disabled and styled as the enemy state was, for any outcome (win, loss, or draw) regardless of whose turn it ended on. When a board is mounted on an already finished game (e.g. returning to the board after watching a replay or reloading), the result panel and its rematch buttons are revealed immediately (`data-revealed="true"` with no 3.8s animation delay), while games ending while the board is mounted continue to wait out the effects layer's lethal and victory/defeat sequence. A new ruling note R4734000 records both presentation behaviors under SPEC §10.10 and R200.

     ```markdown
     ---
     id: R4734000
     title: "A finished game's board stops reading Enemy turn, and a board opened on a finished game shows its result at once (issue #4734)"
     cards: "§10.10, R200, issue #4734"
     proven_in:

       - apps/web/src/game/Game.test.tsx
       - apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx

     **Why.** Once a game was over, two presentation issues degraded the board's clarity (issue #4734):
     1. The End turn button read "Enemy turn" after every game, even a game the player won on their own turn. The turn plate beside it read "Game over", but on portrait viewports on mobile devices, End turn is the only turn wording visible.
     2. When a board mounted on a game already finished (for instance, returning to the match route after watching a replay, or reloading a page on a finished match), the Victory or Defeat panel stayed transparent and ignored pointers for 3.8 seconds (`resultRevealMs()`, 600 ms lethal lead + 3200 ms result sequence).      - `Game` tracks whether the board mounted on an in-progress game (`shown.result === null`). Only when the result arrived on the mounted board (transition from `result === null` to `result !== null`) does `GameResult` wait out `resultRevealMs()`; if the board mounted on an already-finished game, the reveal delay is 0, displaying the result panel with `data-revealed="true"` immediately. Reduced motion and disabled effects continue to reveal with 0 delay ([[R200]], [[§10.10]]).

     - Retaining the 3.8-second delay when mounting on an already finished game: nothing plays in the effects layer on that mount, so the delay served only to block player input (such as Rematch).
     ```

## 6. Risks

- **Animation timing divergence between FxLayer and Result**: `FxLayer` plays the lethal lead and Victory/Defeat cues only on the condition `previousResult === null && view.result !== null`. If `GameResult` used a different condition or waited on initial mount, the panel would either appear over a running animation or stay invisible with nothing playing. By coupling `arrived` strictly to whether the board mounted on an in-progress game (`shown.result === null`), `GameResult` waits if and only if `FxLayer` triggers its cues.
- **Layout shift**: Hiding the End turn button upon game over was rejected because it would shift the rail layout right when the result arrives. Keeping the button visible in its `"over"` state with the same physical dimensions and sunken styling prevents layout jumping.

When an online, daily or co-op game ends on the viewer's own turn (opponent's `concede`, `disconnect`, `draw-accepted` or `match-ceiling`), any half-built play or attack is dropped on the render that shows the result, so the result panel is the only thing on screen: the play's own picker closes, a selected attacker clears, and a drag released afterwards sends nothing. The existing #2924 drop is reused by adding the game's end to the `boardKeyOf` key; no CSS, z-index or engine change, and no ruling (presentation under CLAUDE.md rule 7; the engine already refuses post-end actions per R216).

options.change: Widen this pass to diagnose and fix the stinkyscape-150-run vs Immune-to-Spells Exile interaction (engine/semantics change with its own ruling and tests).

decision.problem: Two of CI's three blocking findings were caused by this change and are now fixed and green. The third — the fuzz Duos seed-5 failure (I21 Spell reached Immune to Spells in a stinkyscape-150 run) — reproduces deterministically, but it also reproduces byte-identically on the base commit with none of this branch in it: same seed, same step 41, same invariant, same cards. This branch's simulation footprint is provably zero (no engine, card-sim, or AI code touched; zero keywords-array changes across 2010 faces; the only sim reads of card text are order-independent; golden replay still folds to 512357ea). So the red gate is a pre-existing engine bug, not something this display-order patch caused. I cannot waive a required gate, and I cannot honestly fix engine targeting semantics inside a words-only keyword-line patch — that fix needs its own ruling, tests, and review. Routing it is a scope call only a person can make.

4696.why: I checked it on main: when a socket drops while it is being seated, the server queues Disconnect ahead of Attach, and both hosts' on_attached then cancel the grace without checking the seat is still connected, so the seat sits empty with no countdown; the fix is small, the bug is confirmed, and it breaks behaviour that §9.5 and the server README promise.

4722.why: It mirrors two refusals POST already returns so the result screen stops offering a rematch that can only fail with 409.

4723.why: It mirrors two refusals the offer already returns so the co-op panel stops showing Play again when pressing it can only fail.

4730.why: Banned queue tickets still pair and strand an opponent today, and the fix extends decided R4019000 with cited code and tests.

4732.why: Confirmed: the #4273 guard in build-wasm.sh greps for a name that the #4283 strip removes, so it can no longer fire; a scratch crate on the pinned toolchain built with the script's settings still traps with the grep finding nothing, the proposed deny(linker_messages) turns that into a link error, and the real C module builds today with no linker messages, so the fix won't break it.

4733.why: Confirmed on main: the practice host clears a finished fight's save (host.rs:468), the dungeon's Menu next to Continue only navigates (FightScreen.tsx:181), and the kept run has nothing marking the fight as played, so a lost or conceded fight gets a free retry, which breaks §15's one lost fight ending the run.

4734.why: Confirmed on main: End turn reads 'Enemy turn' on every finished view (Board.tsx:632-633, 822), and a board mounted on a finished game hides its result for 3.8 s waiting on an effect that FxLayer plays only on a null-to-result change (FxLayer.tsx:464), so these are small fixes to bugs players can see.

4737.why: Confirmed rules bugs on a shipped card where board scopes, Cleave, and enemy permanents treat a card lying on a unit zone as a Unit rather than backrow, violating R4665000.

4743.why: Confirmed on main: boardKeyOf (actions.ts:107-109) keys only on turn, active seat and viewer, so when the opponent concedes or times out on your turn, a play's own picker (Prompt.tsx's outstandingNeed branch, z-index 40) stays open over the Victory panel (z-index 39) and a drag release still sends; adding the result to the key is a one-line fix that reuses the existing #2924 drop.

4761.why: It prices a live mechanic the evaluation scores at zero, with the missing arm confirmed and the value gated by a fork screen.

4770.why: It adds the spec-required R280 preview Edwin is missing, mirroring Quickstriker's proven hook with no rules change.

decided.reason: confirmed.
